entries.summary: Start Here now says what the work needs most: co-editors. The hero shows live seats filled and proposals waiting, with a 'Become a co-editor' button. 'Ways to contribute' opens with 'Co-edit a DP' (how co-editors decide, how to claim or nominate, and the DPs with open seats). The workgroup and book tracks describe proposals going to co-editors on the Review tab instead of promoting Gov Hub drafts, and the 'Patch on Gov Hub' button is hidden. The homepage Start Here panel matches.

entries.title: DP Roundups page centred on co-editors
entries.summary: The Roundups page now leads with the co-editor model. 'Where the work stands' shows live co-editor seats filled, DPs fully staffed and open proposals, and lists the DPs that still need a co-editor, each linked to its workgroup. 'How you can participate' starts with claiming or nominating a co-editor seat. The breakout, reportback and V1 sections describe co-editor decisions on the Review tab. The outdated three-member target and 'not yet reported here' line are gone. Each session page points members to open seats. The per-person seat limit is stated as three.

entries.title: Proposals credited to their named contributors
entries.summary: Astra-reconciled changes posted through the shared Metaweb Academy account showed the Gov Hub account behind that email as author. They are now credited to their first named contributor (BridgeDAO's collective attribution for anonymous CFI submissions, or Astra for Astra-authored corrections). A contributor with two Gov Hub accounts has all proposals on one.
changes: scripts/recredit_proposals.py (box #1, runs inside Gov Hub; dry run by default)

entries.title: Filer: book posts Astra replaced with changes that never reached the book are filed as written
entries.summary: Astra's 2026-09-05 release folded 26 of Phahsa Ras's DP4 posts into its own revised changes, and the filer skipped any post Astra had decided. Those Astra changes were never posted to the book or filed in Gov Hub, so the contributor's work reached nobody. The filer now skips an Astra-decided post only when the Astra change that replaced it was posted; otherwise it files the post as written, credited to its author, with a note naming the unposted Astra change.
changes: scripts/canopi_patch_file_to_govhub.py: astra_canopi_dispositions() carries release and change ids; skip only when a linked change was posted

entries.title: Gov Hub accounts for book authors so their proposals are credited to them
entries.summary: 54 book proposals could not be filed because their authors (mostly reviewers whose emailed feedback was posted for them) had no Gov Hub account. scripts/create_reviewer_accounts.py creates each account from the author's Canopi name and email, with no sign-in attached; their first sign-in with that email links to it.
changes: scripts/create_reviewer_accounts.py (box #1, runs inside Gov Hub; dry run by default)

entries.title: Retire the Process Data workflow
entries.summary: The Process Data GitHub Actions workflow failed on all 24 runs it ever made. The per-submission JSON files it compiled were deleted from the repo on 2025-09-08, and its four scripts each assumed a different folder layout. The site no longer reads its output: challenge-site uses its own src/data, and the web app's submit route writes submissions on the server. Fixing only the paths would have compiled zero submissions over data/compiled/allstructured.json and pushed that to main, so the workflow is removed instead. The scripts stay for running by hand.
changes: Removed .github/workflows/process-data.yml
Rail sync keeps pushing to main with the MAIN_PUSH_DEPLOY_KEY deploy key
data/compiled/ and the scripts in scripts/ are unchanged

entries.title: Anchor audit of every open book proposal; filer fixes
entries.summary: All 289 open book proposals were audited for where they land. 95 Canopi posts and 12 Gov Hub proposals get corrected anchors (scripts and data in scripts/anchor-audit-2026-10-19), three PDPP sections misfiled on DP22 are withdrawn and refiled on DP1, DP4 and DP7, and two duplicates are skipped. The Canopi filer no longer splices inside headings, at the first of several identical anchors, or in reverse order, and can anchor next to formatted lines.
changes: scripts/canopi_patch_file_to_govhub.py: whole heading lines (above a heading goes above its rule), unique anchors, formatted edges, heading-marker patches, whole-passage patches that keep emphasis, skip overrides
scripts/apply_canopi_anchor_fixes.py and scripts/apply_govhub_anchor_fixes.py (box #1, dry run by default, backup/rollback)
scripts/canopi_filing_overrides.json: superseded overrides removed; duplicates skipped
scripts/test_canopi_filer_anchors.py

entries.summary: The Approve and Decline controls on the Review tab appear only for the DP's co-editors; everyone else sees who has approved and a note on how to claim a seat. The site's API and Gov Hub refuse decisions from anyone else.

Only the DP's co-editors see an active Approve button. The workgroups list shows Open Proposals and Readiness on each DP card. entries.title: Astra-reconciled CFI changes are filed as Gov Hub proposals
entries.summary: The Canopi→Gov Hub filer skipped the 95 Astra-reconciled CFI changes on the book, so co-editors could not approve them on Review. It now files them like any other book patch or insert, under the contributor's account, with Astra's rationale and the CFI change id. Review no longer says unfiled posts are filed every 30 minutes; it says when the filer last ran.

entries.title: Review tab: every book patch and insert, with its anchored passage
entries.summary: The workgroup Review tab only read book posts from the DP community, so patches and inserts posted in Canopi's Public Square (most of them, including the Astra-reconciled CFI changes and emailed reviews) were missing: DP1 showed 1 of 9. Each item now shows the passage it is anchored to, whether an insert goes above or below it, and its rationale. Diff highlights the change against that passage; As updated shows the passage as it would read. Open on book Discuss goes to the post itself.

entries.title: Workgroup chat: links to single messages, and notes sent by email
entries.summary: Each workgroup chat message now has its own link. Opening it goes to the chat, finds the message (loading older messages if needed) and highlights it. Activity items for chat posts link to the message itself. Notes a reviewer sent by email and that were posted for them show a 'via email' label, keep their formatting (paragraphs, lists, links), list any attached files with their size, and link the reviewer's name to their Canopi profile when we can find it.

entries.title: Review tab: turn open comments into proposals
entries.summary: Each workgroup's Review tab now lists the reader comments anchored to passages of its chapter, from Gov Hub and book Discuss. A member can have AI draft a proposal from a comment (following the style guide), edit it, and file it to Gov Hub under their own name with the commenter credited; ask the commenter (a reply under Gov Hub comments, or a link to Discuss); or close it as not actionable with a note. Every AI draft is recorded next to the text actually filed, and admins can export them.

entries.title: AI style check for patches and inserts, with an audit trail
entries.summary: Pending patches and inserts on a workgroup's Review tab now get 'Style notes': an AI check against the style guide that names each problem, the guide section it breaks, and a suggested wording. Co-editors can rate the notes helpful or not. The same check is available to Canopi's book composer through a server-to-server endpoint. Every check is recorded with its inputs, model, raw response, timing and the ratings and outcomes that followed, and admins can review and export them under Admin → AI style checks.

entries.title: Review tab shows style-pass proposals; style tasks for workgroups
entries.summary: From 20 October each chapter gets one style-pass proposal holding all its mechanical style-guide fixes (Meta-Layer capitalization, dashes, the '(Non-Normative)' label, § references). The Review tab labels it 'style pass' and lists every line before and after, so co-editors approve or decline it once. Three new weekly tasks cover the judgement calls: making each MUST and SHOULD testable, adding sources, and deciding the style pass.

entries.title: Style guide for the Desirable Properties book
entries.summary: A new page, /style-guide, sets how the book is written so 23 chapters read as one: who we write for, voice, requirement language (MUST/SHOULD/MAY), chapter structure, headings, terms, formatting, cross-references, sources, how to write a patch or insert, and guidance for co-editors. Most rules record what the chapters already do; the rest settle where they disagree. The same rules are available as text for the upcoming AI check of patches and inserts.

entries.intent: Consistent tone and style across chapters, agreed at the 12 Oct 2026 session; the basis for the AI pre-check of manual patches and inserts.

entries.title: Canopi chapter feeds cached and rate-capped
entries.summary: Activity and search read every chapter's Canopi feed on each call. Those reads are now cached for 60 seconds and at most 4 run at once, so the site no longer floods Canopi (about 2,600 requests in 4 minutes on 2026-09-25) and Canopi's sidebar stays fast.
changes: 60 s cache per chapter feed, shared by concurrent callers; failed reads are not cached
At most 4 Canopi feed requests in flight per server process
Test: npm run test:canopi-feed-cache
entries.intent: Stop DP from slowing Canopi for everyone (canopi#32).
